label: sleep
documentation: Waits without blocking other tasks. Rejects with an AbortError when the task is cancelled.

label: nextFrame
documentation: Waits until the next picture frame is shown.

label: every
detail: every(intervalMs: number, handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Runs a handler again and again, waiting intervalMs before each run.

label: after
detail: after(delayMs: number, handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Runs a handler once after a delay, unless it is disposed first.

label: waitUntil
documentation: Waits until a condition gives a truthy value and resolves with it; rejects with a TimeoutError (GS-API-030) when the time is up.

label: retry
detail: retry(times: number, action: (attempt: number) => unknown): Promise<unknown>
documentation: Runs an action and tries again when it throws, up to times more; a cancelled task is not retried.

label: withTimeout
detail: withTimeout(timeoutMs: number, action: (context: TaskContext) => unknown): Promise<unknown>
documentation: Runs an action with a time limit: when the time is up its signal aborts and the Promise rejects with a TimeoutError (GS-API-030).

label: parallel
documentation: Runs several things at the same time and waits for all of them.

label: sequence
documentation: Runs several things one after another, in order, waiting for each before it starts the next.

label: multiGate
detail: multiGate(name: string, times: number, loop: boolean, random: boolean, ...work: Work[]): Promise<unknown>
documentation: Runs the next of several functions each time it is called, in turn or in random order, and one more function after they have all run.

label: race
documentation: Runs several things at the same time and waits for the first to finish.

label: doOnce
documentation: Runs an action only the first time it is called with this name.

label: resetOnce
documentation: Lets doOnce run the action with this name again.

label: doN
documentation: Says yes for the first times calls with this name, and no after that, until resetDoN with the same name.

label: resetDoN
documentation: Lets doN with this name pass that many times again.

label: gate
documentation: A named gate that lets an action through only while it is open.

label: flipFlop
documentation: Gives "A" and "B" in turn, starting with "A", for each name.

label: throttle
detail: throttle(intervalMs: number, action: (...values: unknown[]) => unknown): (...values: unknown[]) => unknown
documentation: Makes a function that runs the action at most once per interval and ignores calls in between.

label: debounce
detail: debounce(waitMs: number, action: (...values: unknown[]) => unknown): (...values: unknown[]) => void
documentation: Makes a function that runs the action only after the calls have stopped for waitMs.

label: stopwatch
documentation: A stopwatch that starts now.

label: point
documentation: A position on the picture, as ratios.

label: defineInterface
documentation: Makes an interface, or gives back the one with this name, so components of different kinds can answer the same call: list it in static implements of their classes, then mapping.all(it) or it.all() gives every component that implements it. Throws GS-API-011 for a name that is not a string or is empty.

label: Task
documentation: The base class of a task. The task.ts of a task exports a class that extends it: static params lists its settings and run() does the work.

label: controls
documentation: The components of the profile in use, by id; empty without a phone. In a task they are the components of the profile the phone uses now, and are made again from the new profile when the phone switches.

label: vars
documentation: The variables of the profile in use, by id; empty without a phone. In a task they follow the phone's profile, as controls do.

label: keys
documentation: Keys, mouse buttons and gamepad buttons by name: keys.F, keys.Space, keys.MouseLeft, keys.GamepadA.

label: globals
documentation: Values shared by every profile and task on this phone.

label: machine
detail: machine: <S extends string>(states: { readonly [K in S]: (to: MachineTo<S>) => MachineStep | void | Promise<MachineStep | void> }, options?: MachineOptions<S>) => Promise<void>
documentation: Runs a state machine: each member of states is a state, an async function that receives to and returns to.<next state>(reason) to move on, or nothing to end the machine. The first member is the start unless options.start names another. The editor shows the state it is in and every transition with its reason. Throws GS-API-008 when states is not an object of functions and GS-API-002 for an unknown start.

label: ext
documentation: The system nodes that native extensions add: ext.<extension>.<node>(...) runs a node at once and gives its result. <extension> is the extension id with each part in lowerCamelCase, so the nodes of gamescrcpy.pc-clock are ext.gamescrcpy.pcClock. Throws GS-API-060 when the extension is not on, GS-API-061 for values of the wrong type, GS-API-062 when the node fails, GS-API-063 naming a permission the extension lacks and GS-API-064 when the node takes longer than 100 ms. A job the extension offers, ext.<extension>.<job>({ ... }), starts at once with its arguments by name and gives an ExtensionJob; starting throws GS-API-060, GS-API-061 and GS-API-063 as a node does, and GS-API-067 when the extension runs as many of its jobs as it may. ext.call() and ext.provide() call and answer the services that extensions offer each other.

label: log
documentation: Lines in the script console, with the task that wrote them.

label: log.info
documentation: Writes an information line to the script console.

label: log.warn
documentation: Writes a warning line to the script console.

label: log.error
documentation: Writes an error line to the script console.

label: log.time
documentation: Starts a timer with this name; log.timeEnd() with the same name writes how long it has been running.

label: log.timeEnd
documentation: Writes an information line with the milliseconds since log.time() with this name and gives that number; with no such timer it writes a warning line and gives null.

label: time
documentation: The script clock.

label: time.now
documentation: Milliseconds since the scripts started; virtual time when replaying a recording.

label: touch
documentation: Touches on the phone picture. Positions are ratios of the picture: (0, 0) top left, (1, 1) bottom right.

label: touch.tap
detail: touch.tap(x: number | PicturePoint, y?: number, durationMs?: number): Action<void>
documentation: Taps the picture at a position; resolves when the finger is lifted, which is at once if the task is cancelled.

label: touch.longPress
detail: touch.longPress(x: number | PicturePoint, y?: number, durationMs?: number): Action<void>
documentation: Presses and holds the picture at a position, then lifts the finger.

label: touch.swipe
detail: touch.swipe(fromX: number | PicturePoint, fromY: number | PicturePoint, toX?: number, toY?: number, durationMs?: number): Action<void>
documentation: Swipes from one position to another; resolves when it ends. If the task is cancelled, the finger is lifted where it is.

label: touch.down
detail: touch.down(x: number | PicturePoint, y?: number): Finger
documentation: Puts a finger down and keeps it there until up() or the end of the task that put it down.

label: touch.pinch
detail: touch.pinch(center: PicturePoint, from: number, to: number, durationMs?: number): Action<void>
documentation: Pinches with two fingers around a position: from is how far apart they start and to how far apart they end, as ratios of the picture width, so a growing distance zooms in. If the task is cancelled, both fingers are lifted.

label: touch.releaseAll
documentation: Lifts every finger the script has put down.

label: device
documentation: The phone this script runs on.

label: device.info
documentation: The phone this script runs on: model, Android version, screen size and rotation.

label: device.back
documentation: Presses the phone's Back key.

label: device.home
documentation: Presses the phone's Home key.

label: device.recents
documentation: Opens the list of recent apps.

label: device.menu
documentation: Presses the phone's Menu key.

label: device.power
documentation: Presses the phone's Power key.

label: device.volumeUp
documentation: Turns the phone's volume up one step.

label: device.volumeDown
documentation: Turns the phone's volume down one step.

label: device.mute
documentation: Mutes or unmutes the phone.

label: device.notifications
documentation: Pulls down the phone's notification shade, as the More menu of the mirror window's toolbar does; true once the phone is asked, false when it cannot be asked now, such as while GameScrcpy reconnects to it. When the phone does not allow it, its mirror window says so. The shade stays down when the logic stops.

label: device.quickSettings
documentation: Opens the phone's quick settings, as the More menu of the mirror window's toolbar does; true once the phone is asked, false when it cannot be asked now. They stay open when the logic stops.

label: device.collapsePanels
documentation: Closes the phone's notification shade and quick settings, as the More menu of the mirror window's toolbar does; true once the phone is asked, false when it cannot be asked now.

label: device.pressKey
documentation: Presses and releases an Android key on the phone.

label: device.type
documentation: Types text into the box that has the focus on the phone.

label: device.launch
documentation: Starts an app on the phone; false when the phone cannot be asked now.

label: device.screenOff
documentation: Turns the phone's screen off while mirroring goes on.

label: device.screenOn
documentation: Turns the phone's screen back on.

label: device.foregroundApp
documentation: The app in front on the phone, when the phone has said which.

label: device.onForegroundApp
detail: device.onForegroundApp(handler: (event: TaskContext & ForegroundApp) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time another app comes to the front.

label: device.onRotate
detail: device.onRotate(handler: (event: TaskContext & DeviceInfo) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the phone's screen turns.

label: device.connected
documentation: Whether the phone is connected now; false while GameScrcpy is reconnecting to it. Taps, swipes, key presses and other actions made while it is not connected wait and happen once it is back; the logic and tasks go on, and stop only when reconnecting is given up.

label: device.onDisconnect
detail: device.onDisconnect(handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the connection to the phone drops and reconnecting begins.

label: device.onReconnect
detail: device.onReconnect(handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the phone is connected again after it dropped.

label: device.onInputBox
detail: device.onInputBox(handler: (event: TaskContext & InputBox) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time an input box opens, changes or closes on the phone. It needs the GameScrcpy Companion input method on the phone; without it, and in replays, it never fires.

label: device.rotate
documentation: Keeps the phone's screen upright or sideways, or lets it follow the phone again, like the screen direction in the mirror toolbar; false when the phone cannot be asked now.

label: clipboard
documentation: The phone's clipboard, not the computer's.

label: clipboard.read
documentation: Reads the text on the phone's clipboard, an empty string when it holds no text; null when the phone cannot share its clipboard now, such as when it is not mirroring or mirrors an app on its own display, and in replays.

label: clipboard.write
documentation: Puts text on the phone's clipboard; the computer's clipboard stays as it is. Resolves with true when the text was sent to the phone, false when the phone cannot share its clipboard now and in replays.

label: mapping
documentation: The controls of the profile in use, by id; the script's output never feeds back into its input.

label: mapping.controls
documentation: The controls of the profile in use, with their ids and whether they are on.

label: mapping.get
documentation: The component with this id, or null.

label: mapping.all
detail: mapping.all(type?: ComponentType | Interface<unknown> | { readonly prototype: Component } | { readonly component?: Component }): Component[]
documentation: All components of the profile, or those of one type, of one class or with one interface.

label: mapping.trigger
documentation: Presses and releases a control as if its key were tapped; the script's own output never triggers scripts.

label: mapping.hold
documentation: Holds a control down for a while, then releases it; released early if the task is cancelled.

label: mapping.setEnabled
documentation: Turns a control on or off until the script ends or the profile changes; this ends a binding of the control's enabled.

label: mapping.on
documentation: Turns key mapping on for this phone.

label: mapping.off
documentation: Turns key mapping off for this phone, so keys go to the phone as they are.

label: mapping.toggle
documentation: Turns key mapping on or off for this phone.

label: mapping.isOn
documentation: Whether key mapping is on for this phone.

label: hints
documentation: The key hints drawn on the phone picture.

label: hints.show
documentation: Shows the key hints on the picture.

label: hints.hide
documentation: Hides the key hints on the picture.

label: hints.toggle
documentation: Shows or hides the key hints.

label: hints.setOpacity
documentation: Sets how solid the key hints are.

label: hints.reveal
documentation: While on, every key hint of this phone is drawn at full opacity, even when the hints are hidden or faded; typing on the phone still hides them. Each logic and each task has its own switch, which turns off when that logic or task stops.

label: profile
documentation: The profile in use on this phone.

label: profile.current
documentation: The profile this script belongs to.

label: profile.switchTo
documentation: Switches this phone to another profile by id or name; this script stops and that profile's logic starts.

label: profile.next
documentation: Switches this phone to the next profile in the library.

label: profile.previous
documentation: Switches this phone to the previous profile in the library.

label: profile.save
documentation: Asks in the phone's mirror window whether to keep the changes this logic made to its components (each shown as old and new value) in the profile, and resolves with whether they were saved. Saving reloads the profile and starts the logic again, as saving in the key editor does. Resolves with false at once when nothing was changed, while the key editor is open, for a profile that is not in the library, and in a task.

label: store
documentation: Values this script keeps between runs (up to 1 MiB of JSON).

label: store.get
documentation: Reads a value this script stored earlier, or undefined.

label: store.set
documentation: Stores a value that stays after the script and the program restart.

label: store.remove
documentation: Removes a stored value.

label: store.keys
documentation: The names of all stored values.

label: ui
documentation: Messages, questions and drawings in the phone's mirror window.

label: ui.toast
documentation: Shows a short message in the phone's mirror window.

label: ui.confirm
documentation: Asks a yes or no question in the phone's mirror window and resolves with the answer; cancelling the task closes the question.

label: ui.choose
detail: ui.choose(question: string, choices: string[]): Promise<number | null>
documentation: Offers choices in the phone's mirror window and resolves with the index chosen, or null when it is closed.

label: ui.ask
detail: ui.ask(question: string, options?: AskOptions): Promise<string | null>
documentation: Asks for a line of text in the phone's mirror window and resolves with it, or null when it is closed.

label: ui.box
detail: ui.box(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, options?: BoxOptions): Drawing
documentation: Draws a box on the phone picture until it is disposed, its duration ends or the task that drew it ends.

label: ui.text
detail: ui.text(x: number, y: number, text: string, options?: TextOptions): Drawing
documentation: Writes text on the phone picture until it is disposed, its duration ends or the task that drew it ends.

label: ui.mark
detail: ui.mark(x: number, y: number, options?: MarkOptions): Drawing
documentation: Marks a point on the phone picture with a ring and a dot until it is disposed, its duration ends or the task that drew it ends; the label shows to the right of the ring.

label: ui.image
detail: ui.image(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, region?: Region | RegionName, options?: BoxOptions): Drawing
documentation: Shows a picture on the phone picture in a thin frame until it is disposed, its duration ends or the task that drew it ends. An image from vision.capture() that is no longer kept shows nothing.

label: ui.progress
detail: ui.progress(title: string | null, value?: number): void
documentation: Shows a card at the top of the phone picture with the title, a bar and the percentage. Each logic and each task has one card: calling again updates it, and it goes away with ui.progress(null) or when the logic or task stops.

label: ui.notify
documentation: Shows a Windows notification; clicking it opens the phone's mirror window. Each logic and each task shows at most one every 10 seconds; false means this one was not shown.

label: ui.panel
documentation: Gives a panel of this extension, declared in contributes.panels: a side panel of the mirror window, a page of the main window, a section of Settings, part of the extension's settings window, the settings of a device it adds, or what its toolbar button opens. GameScrcpy draws the tree given to render() with its own controls; no interface code of the extension runs.

label: ui.menu
documentation: Puts this extension's group of items into the right-click menu on the phone picture, in place of the last ones; ui.menu.on("select", handler) hears the item picked.

label: ui.status
documentation: Gives a status widget of this extension, declared in contributes.panels: a little text, icons and progress shown with the status of the mirror window.

label: ui.toolbar
documentation: Gives a toolbar button of this extension, declared in contributes.panels with where "toolbar": a button on the mirror window's toolbar with the declared title and icon while this logic runs. A click sends click; once ui.panel() of the same name has drawn a tree, the click also opens it under the button.

label: ui.contextMenu
documentation: Gives a menu of this extension, declared in contributes.panels with where "contextMenu": its items are added to the More menu of the cards its on names, device cards and profile cards.

label: ui.tray
documentation: Gives this extension's group of items in the tray menu, declared in contributes.panels with where "tray".

label: input
documentation: What the user holds and points at, readable only while the phone's mirror window is in front.

label: input.source
documentation: An input source of this logic, such as a device it reads: the keys it presses and the axes it moves reach the phone's key mapping as the input Ext.<extension id>.<name>.<key>, or Ext.mine.<name>.<key> for your own logic, which profiles bind like any key. While the key editor waits for a key, a press is taken as that key.

label: input.cursor
documentation: Where the pointer is over the phone picture, as ratios; null when the phone's mirror window is not in front or the pointer is outside the picture.

label: input.isDown
documentation: Whether a key or mouse button is held; always false when the phone's mirror window is not in front.

label: hardware
documentation: Serial ports, USB HID devices and Bluetooth LE devices the user allows. Every logic, your own too, can only open the devices the user ticked; the logic of an extension also needs the permission hardware.

label: hardware.request
documentation: Shows the user a list of the connected devices of that kind; the user ticks the ones this logic may use. Resolves with every ticked device, those allowed before included, or with an empty list when the user cancels. Bluetooth devices are looked for while the list is open.

label: hardware.list
documentation: The devices this logic may open, connected or not; present says whether each one is connected now.

label: hardware.open
detail: hardware.open(id: string, options?: SerialOptions): Promise<SerialDevice | HidDevice | BleDevice>
documentation: Opens an allowed device; a device can be open only once in GameScrcpy. A device opened in a task closes when the task ends, one opened at the top level when the logic stops.

label: hardware.forget
documentation: Gives up the permission to use a device, as its remove button on the Extensions page does; the device closes if it is open.

label: hardware.claim
documentation: Tells other extensions and GameScrcpy's own sessions that this logic is using the hardware, so that they leave it alone. Resolves with false when someone else holds it. Devices opened with hardware.open() are claimed while they are open. A claim made in a task ends with the task, one made at the top level when the logic stops.

label: hardware.release
documentation: Lets go of hardware claimed with hardware.claim().

label: net
documentation: Connections from programs on this computer over HTTP on 127.0.0.1; the logic of an extension needs the permission network.listen.

label: net.listen
detail: net.listen(port: number, handler: (request: NetRequest) => NetAnswer | Promise<NetAnswer>, options?: NetListenOptions): Promise<NetServer>
documentation: Opens an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 that programs on this computer, such as Stream Deck or OBS, can call; nothing from other computers can reach it. Each request goes to the handler, which answers with an object, a text or nothing (204); a handler that throws answers 500. A server opened in a task closes when the task ends, one opened at the top level when the logic stops.

label: speech
documentation: Reading text aloud and listening for voice commands, with Windows or an engine that an extension provides; the logic of an extension needs the permission speech.listen to listen.

label: speech.say
documentation: Reads a text aloud with the engine, voice, rate and volume set in Settings, Audio, unless the options pick others. Each engine reads one text at a time and the others wait their turn. Resolves with true once the text has been read, and with false when it is cut off by interrupt, speech.stop(), the task being cancelled or the logic stopping.

label: speech.stop
documentation: Stops what this logic is reading and drops the texts it has waiting.

label: speech.engines
documentation: The speech engines: Windows, and those that extensions provide, with what each can do.

label: speech.voices
documentation: The voices of an engine.

label: speech.listen
detail: speech.listen(phrases: readonly string[] | null, handler: (heard: TaskContext & SpeechHeard) => void | Promise<void>, options?: SpeechListenOptions): Promise<SpeechListener>
documentation: Listens to the microphone for voice commands with the engine and language set in Settings, Audio, unless the options pick others. Each command heard with at least the confidence asked for (0.6 by default) runs the handler as a task, one after another. A listener opened in a task closes when the task ends, one opened at the top level when the logic stops; it also closes when its engine stops, and the log says why.

label: window
documentation: The phone's mirror window.

label: window.focused
documentation: Whether the phone's mirror window is the active window, the one that gets the keyboard; false while another window is in front or the mirror window is closed.

label: window.onFocus
detail: window.onFocus(handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the phone's mirror window becomes the active window.

label: window.onBlur
detail: window.onBlur(handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the phone's mirror window stops being the active window, such as when another window comes to the front.

label: vision
documentation: Finding pictures in the phone's picture: the next frame, or the picture already shown when none comes within 0.25 s.

label: vision.find
detail: vision.find(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, options?: FindOptions): Promise<Found | null>
documentation: Looks for a picture in the next frame, or in the picture already shown when no new frame comes within 0.25 s, and resolves with the best place; null when it is not there, or when there is no picture before the timeout.

label: vision.findAll
detail: vision.findAll(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, options?: FindOptions): Promise<Found[]>
documentation: Looks for every place a picture appears in the next frame (or the picture already shown), best first, without overlapping matches.

label: vision.findColor
detail: vision.findColor(color: ColorName | HexColor, options?: ColorOptions): Promise<Found | null>
documentation: Looks for a color in the next frame (or the picture already shown) and resolves with its largest group of pixels: a pixel matches when its red, green and blue each differ from the color by at most tolerance times 255, and matching pixels that touch, diagonally too, form one group. x and y are the center of the group's bounding box, width and height its size, and score the share of matching pixels in that box; null when no pixel matches, or when there is no picture before the timeout.

label: vision.pickColor
detail: vision.pickColor(at: PicturePoint, options?: PixelOptions): Promise<HexColor | null>
documentation: Reads the color of one pixel in the next frame, or in the picture already shown when no new frame comes within 0.25 s, and resolves with it written "#RRGGBB"; null when there is no picture before the timeout.

label: vision.matchColor
detail: vision.matchColor(at: PicturePoint, color: ColorName | HexColor, options?: PixelMatchOptions): Promise<boolean>
documentation: Checks one pixel in the next frame (or the picture already shown) against a color: true when its red, green and blue each differ from the color by at most tolerance times 255; false when they do not, or when there is no picture before the timeout.

label: vision.waitFor
detail: vision.waitFor(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, options?: WaitOptions): Promise<Found | null>
documentation: Looks for a picture again and again until it appears and resolves with where it is; null when it has not appeared within timeoutMs.

label: vision.waitGone
detail: vision.waitGone(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, options?: WaitOptions): Promise<boolean>
documentation: Looks for a picture again and again until it is gone; true when it went away, false when it was still there after timeoutMs.

label: vision.findAndTap
detail: vision.findAndTap(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, options?: FindOptions): Promise<Found | null>
documentation: Looks for a picture once and taps the middle of the best place; resolves with where it was, or null without tapping when it is not there.

label: vision.watch
detail: vision.watch(image: TemplateName | ImagePath | CapturedImage, onAppear: (event: TaskContext & Found) => void | Promise<void>, onGone?: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: WatchOptions): Subscription
documentation: Keeps looking for a picture, starting onAppear each time it appears and onGone each time it goes away, each run as its own task; dispose() stops looking.

label: vision.capture
detail: vision.capture(region?: Region | RegionName, options?: PixelOptions): Promise<CapturedImage | null>
documentation: Takes part of the next frame, or of the picture already shown when no new frame comes within 0.25 s, as an image: look for it later with find(), show it with ui.image() or keep it with save(). Resolves with null when there is no picture before the timeout. A script keeps its 8 latest images; older ones can no longer be used.

label: vision.changed
detail: vision.changed(region?: Region | RegionName, options?: ChangeOptions): Promise<boolean>
documentation: Looks at part of the next frame (or the picture already shown) and compares it with how it looked the last time changed() looked at the same region: true when it changed. The first look only remembers it and resolves with false, as does a look without a picture before the timeout.

label: vision.onChange
detail: vision.onChange(region: Region | RegionName, handler: (event: TaskContext) => void | Promise<void>, options?: OnChangeOptions): Subscription
documentation: Keeps looking at part of the picture and starts a task each time it changed since the last look; the first look only remembers it. dispose() stops looking.

label: vision.readText
documentation: Reads the text in the next frame, or in the picture already shown when no new frame comes within 0.25 s, with the text recognition that comes with Windows, and resolves with each line and where it is; null when there is no picture before the timeout. Chinese and Japanese characters are joined without spaces, other words with one. Name the language the game is written in: Chinese recognition reads English words poorly and English recognition cannot read Chinese. Reading a whole picture can take a few tenths of a second, so give a region when you can.

label: vision.findText
detail: vision.findText(text: string, options?: ReadTextOptions): Promise<Found | null>
documentation: Reads the text in the next frame (or the picture already shown) and resolves with where a line says it: a line that says only that comes first, then the first line from the top that contains it, ignoring capitals and spaces. The place covers the words that say it and score is always 1; null when no line says it, or when there is no picture before the timeout.

label: vision.engines
documentation: The recognition engines: "system", the text recognition that comes with Windows, and those that extensions provide, with what each recognizes.

label: vision.recognize
detail: vision.recognize(engine: string, kind: VisionKind, region?: Region | RegionName, params?: VisionParams): Promise<readonly VisionResult[] | null>
documentation: Recognizes text ("ocr"), things ("detect") or what the picture shows ("classify") with an engine, in the next frame or in the picture already shown when no new frame comes within 0.25 s, and resolves with what it found, in the order the engine gives: x and y are the middle and width and height the size, as ratios of the whole picture, and confidence goes from 0 to 1. Resolves with null when there is no picture within 2 seconds. An engine works on one picture at a time and stops waiting for an extension's engine after 5 seconds. The logic of an extension needs the permission device.screen.

label: vision.engine
documentation: An engine by its id, with read(), detect() and classify() as short ways to call recognize(); the id is checked only when it is used.

label: res.path

label: text.lower

label: mcp
documentation: Tools that the app script of an extension offers to AI clients over the local MCP connection.

label: mcp.tool
detail: mcp.tool(name: string, spec: McpToolSpec, handler: (input: any, event: TaskContext) => unknown): Subscription
documentation: Offers a function of this extension to AI clients as a tool of the local MCP connection. The user confirms each call, as for running a script on a phone. The tool is gone when the subscription is disposed or the logic stops.

label: events
documentation: Events of GameScrcpy itself, such as a phone connecting, and events that the native DLL of an extension sends to the extension's own logic and panels and to the logic of the extensions that depend on it.

label: events.on
detail: events.on(topic: string, handler: (event: TaskContext & { readonly topic: string; readonly value: StoreValue }) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time an event of the topic comes. GameScrcpy's own topics and their values: device.connected and device.disconnected { phone, name }, session.started { phone, name }, session.ended { phone, name, failed }, profile.applied { phone, name, profile, profileName }, app.foreground { phone, name, package, game }, orientation.changed { phone, name, rotation } in quarter turns, recording.started { phone, name, path }, recording.ended { phone, name, path, durationMs }, window.focused { phone, name, window: "mirror" or "grid", focused }, extension.enabled and extension.disabled { id, name, version }, and settings.changed { keys, values, extension, device }; phone is the phone's serial and name the name it shows, and values holds the new language and look settings among keys. Your own logic hears all of them. The logic of an extension hears extension.enabled, extension.disabled and settings.changed, which then tells only of its own settings and the language and look settings, and a session script also hears its own phone; the other phones, and app and task scripts, need the permission events.app. Any other topic is one the native DLL of this extension sends, which only the extension's own logic and panels and the logic of the extensions that depend on it hear; written "<extension id>:<topic>", it is one the DLL of an extension that this one lists in its dependencies sends. Of each topic a listener gets the first 100 events in a second at once and the rest of that second merged into the last one.

label: ai
documentation: Questions from logic to the AI service set up in Settings, AI; they work only while Let logic call AI is on there.

label: ai.ask
detail: ai.ask(question: string, options?: AiAskOptions): Promise<string | null>
documentation: Asks the AI service set up in Settings, AI, the one the assistant in the editor uses, and resolves with the text of its answer; null when it answers without text, when a picture is asked for and the phone has shown none yet, and in replays, which ask nothing. With picture, the phone's picture or a part of it goes along, made smaller so its long side is at most 1024 pixels. It works only while Let logic call AI is on there: each question spends your quota, and each logic may ask at most 10 times a minute. Cancelling the task stops waiting.

label: media
documentation: The phone's picture as frames, for analysis and AI; the logic of an extension needs the permission media.read.

label: media.frames
detail: media.frames(handler: (frame: TaskContext & { readonly image: CapturedImage; readonly time: number }) => void | Promise<void>, options?: MediaFrameOptions): Subscription
documentation: Hands the phone's picture to a handler: the frame shown when it starts, then new ones, at most fps a second (2 by default), made smaller so that the long side is at most size pixels (640 by default), and cut to region when one is given. The image is a CapturedImage as vision.capture() gives; it stays usable while its handler runs and until two newer frames came. Frames taken in a task stop when the task ends, ones taken at the top level when the logic stops.

label: ui.menu.on
detail: ui.menu.on(type: "select", handler: (event: UiEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time an item of this extension's group in the right-click menu is picked.

label: Component.id
documentation: The control id from the profile; stays the same when the control is renamed.

label: Component.name
documentation: The name shown in the editor.

label: Component.position
documentation: Where the component sits on the picture, as ratios, for the phone's picture when the logic started; it follows moveTo(). null for a component made in logic with new.

label: Component.type
documentation: The kind of component, such as "tap", "wasd" or "camera".

label: Component.props
documentation: The component's settings: from profile.json, or for a component made in logic its static props with the values given to it (keys become Key objects, positions points and component ids components).

label: Component.key
documentation: Its main key, such as "KeyF" or "Mouse.Right"; null when it has none.

label: Component.inputs
documentation: Every key of the component by slot, such as { up: "KeyW" }.

label: Component.hint
documentation: Its key hint on the picture.

label: Component.enabled
documentation: Whether the control reacts to its keys. Setting it lasts until the script stops or the profile changes, and ends a binding made with bind().

label: Component.enable
documentation: Turns the component on (the same as enabled = true).

label: Component.disable
documentation: Turns the component off.

label: Component.toggle
documentation: Turns the component on or off.

label: Component.active
documentation: Whether its key is held down now.

label: Component.pressedAt
documentation: When its key went down (time.now()), or null when it is up.

label: Component.heldMs
documentation: How long its key has been held, in milliseconds; 0 when it is up.

label: Component.touching
documentation: Whether it has a finger on the phone's screen now.

label: Component.trigger
documentation: Presses and releases the control with its own behavior; the script's own output never triggers scripts.

label: Component.hold
documentation: Holds the control down for a while, then releases it; released early if the task is cancelled. Throws GS-API-003 when the duration is not more than 0 and at most 60000.

label: Component.press
documentation: Puts its finger down and keeps it there until release().

label: Component.release
documentation: Lifts its finger.

label: Component.reset
documentation: Lifts all its fingers and puts it back at rest: a stick back to the middle, a view back to its anchor.

label: Component.moveTo
detail: moveTo(x: number | PicturePoint, y?: number): void
documentation: Moves the component and its key hint to another place on the picture until the logic stops or the profile changes; a finger already down stays where it is, and profile.save() can keep the new place. Throws GS-API-002 for a place outside the picture and GS-API-036 for a component made in logic with new.

label: Component.moveBy
documentation: Moves the component by picture ratios, as moveTo() does.

label: Component.resetPosition
documentation: Puts the component back where the profile has it.

label: Component.resetProps
documentation: Puts back everything the logic changed on this component: its place, rate, duration, radius and sensitivity.

label: Component.bind
documentation: Keeps a property computed from states: compute runs at once and again whenever a state it read last time changes, also when the script changes it. Only "enabled" can be bound. Disposing the binding, or the end of the task that made it, puts the property back to its value from before the binding; binding it again takes over without putting it back, and setting it directly, or with mapping.setEnabled, ends the binding. Throws GS-API-031 for another property, GS-API-008 for a compute that is not a function and GS-API-032 when compute returns a Promise. Later, a compute that throws is reported and keeps the last value, and one that returns a Promise is reported with GS-API-032 and ends the binding as dispose() does.

label: Component.onPress
detail: onPress(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: KeyListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the control's key goes down. In the profile's logic it takes the key of a tap, hold, long press, turbo, swipe or multi-press control unless consume is false (KeyListenOptions). Throws GS-API-008 for a handler that is not a function, GS-API-009 for an unknown again rule and GS-API-011 for a consume that is not true or false.

label: Component.onRelease
detail: onRelease(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: KeyListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time the control's key comes up. It takes the key as onPress does.

label: Component.whileHeld
detail: whileHeld(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: KeyListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task when the control's key goes down and cancels it when the key comes up. It takes the key as onPress does.

label: Component.onEnabled
detail: onEnabled(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time it is turned on.

label: Component.onDisabled
detail: onDisabled(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time it is turned off.

label: Component.onTouchStart
detail: onTouchStart(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time it puts a finger on the screen.

label: Component.onTouchEnd
detail: onTouchEnd(handler: (event: ControlEvent) => void | Promise<void>, options?: ListenOptions): Subscription
documentation: Starts a task each time it lifts its last finger.

label: Component.setup
documentation: For a component made in logic: runs once after it is created; set up its listeners here. Create components at the top level of the logic so these listeners last.

label: Component.event

label: Component.child
detail: child<T extends Component>(kind: { readonly component?: T }): T
documentation: In a field of a component class: one of its child components, a built-in component the editor places with it and moves with it, such as cancel = this.child(Tap) or skills = [this.child(Skill), this.child(Skill)]. label: Component.finger

label: Hint.show

label: Hint.hide

label: Hint.setText

label: Hint.moveTo
detail: moveTo(x: number | PicturePoint, y?: number): void

label: Hint.flash

label: Hint.reset
documentation: Puts the hint back as the profile has it.

label: Tap.tap

label: Tap.tapTimes

label: Swipe.resetDuration

label: Stick.moving

label: Extensions.call
detail: call<T = StoreValue>(service: string, args?: StoreValue): Promise<T>
documentation: Calls a service of an extension, named "<extension id>/<service>" as its manifest declares it in contributes.services, with arguments that its input schema accepts, and gives the result, which its output schema checks. The logic of an extension may call the services of the extensions it lists in dependencies, optional ones too, and its own; your own logic may call any service of an extension that is on. Cancelling the task cancels the call. Throws GS-API-146 when no extension that is on offers the service or its app script has not provided it within 10 seconds, GS-API-147 when this extension does not depend on the one that offers it, GS-API-148 when the arguments or the result do not match the schemas or are not JSON of at most 252 KiB, and GS-API-149 with the service's own message when it fails, or when it takes longer than 10 seconds.

label: Extensions.provide
detail: provide<A = any>(name: string, handler: (args: A, context: ServiceContext) => StoreValue | void | Promise<StoreValue | void>): Subscription
documentation: Answers the calls of a service that the extension declares in contributes.services with this app script as its script. Each call runs as a task of its own with the permissions that both the calling extension and this one have; what the handler returns is the result (nothing gives null), and when it throws the call fails with its message. Providing the same name again replaces the handler; dispose() stops answering. Throws GS-API-145 when the extension does not declare the service for this script, and GS-API-008 when the handler is not a function.

documentation: The values for a new component's static props, with an optional id and whether it starts on.

label: ComponentProp
documentation: A property declared in static props with prop.key, prop.position, prop.number, prop.text, prop.toggle or prop.component.

label: PropOptions
documentation: How a component property is labelled.

label: McpToolSpec
documentation: What an MCP tool of an extension does, in a sentence or two for the AI, and the JSON Schema of its input: an object of type object of at most 16 KiB; without one the tool takes an empty object.

label: NumberPropOptions
documentation: How a number property is labelled, and the smallest and largest value its box in the property panel takes.

label: ParamOptions
documentation: How a task setting shows on the Tasks page: its label, and for numbers the smallest and largest value.

label: AndroidKey
documentation: The Android keys a script can press.

label: DeviceInfo
documentation: The phone: model name, Android version, screen size in pixels and rotation in quarter turns.

label: ComponentType
documentation: The 13 kinds of component.

label: MachineStep
documentation: A move to another state, made by to.<state>(reason) and returned from a state of machine().

label: MachineTo<S>
documentation: What a state of machine() receives: one function per state that makes the move to it, with an optional reason the editor shows on the transition.

label: MachineOptions<S>
documentation: The name the editor shows for a state machine, and the state it starts in (the first one when left out).

label: Interface<T>
documentation: An interface made with defineInterface(): its name, and all(), every component of the profile whose class lists it in static implements, so logic can tell each of them at once.

label: BuiltInClass<T, O>
documentation: A built-in component class. A component of yours that extends it is placed as that built-in component and presses the screen just as it does; the event methods of O that the class writes run each time the event comes, as well. T is the type its components have in controls.

label: ControlInfo
documentation: A control of the profile in use.

label: VarValue
documentation: What a variable holds.

label: StoreValue
documentation: A value the store can keep.

label: ExtensionJob<T>
documentation: A job that a native extension runs, such as writing firmware. result settles when it ends and throws GS-API-065 when it fails and GS-API-066 when it is cancelled; onProgress hears how far it got, fraction from 0 to 1 or -1 when it cannot tell, at most 20 times a second; onLog hears its lines, level 0 information, 1 warning, 2 error; onOutput hears the parts of its result that it hands over while it runs, such as each device a scan finds; follow hears the progress, waits for the job and then runs done with the result or failed with the error, and without failed a failure throws as result does; cancel asks it to stop. It is cancelled when the script stops.

label: ServiceContext
documentation: What the handler of a service gets besides the arguments: the id of the extension that calls it ("" for the user's own logic), the permissions the call runs with, which are those that both extensions have, and the signal that aborts when the caller cancels or the call takes longer than 10 seconds.

label: ListenOptions
documentation: What happens when the event comes again while the last task it started is still running: ignore it (default), restart (cancel the running task first), stop (only cancel the running task), queue (run after it) or parallel (run both).

label: KeyListenOptions
documentation: The options of a control's key events: again as for other events, and consume. With consume true (the default), the profile's logic takes the key of a tap, hold, long press, turbo, swipe or multi-press control it listens to: pressing the key no longer touches the phone, and the control touches only when the logic calls it, such as with press() or tap(), a few milliseconds later than its own touch would. consume: false keeps the control's own touch, which comes before the handler runs. Only the profile's own logic takes keys: tasks, extension scripts and scripts an AI client runs only listen, the event methods a component class overrides keep the built-in touch, and other controls always keep working.

label: Subscription
documentation: A listener; dispose() stops it. Listeners made inside a task stop when that task ends, those made at module top level last as long as the script.

label: UntilOptions
documentation: How long until() waits for its condition after each try of the action, in milliseconds (5000 by default, from 1 to 600000), and how many more times it does the action when the condition does not come true in time (0 by default, at most 10).

label: Action<T>
documentation: What an action returns: a Promise that resolves when the action is done, with until(), which then checks the condition once per frame and resolves with its first truthy value, doing the action again, as often as retry allows, when it does not come true in time. The condition may return a Promise, as vision.find() does. until() rejects with a TimeoutError (GS-API-030) when the tries run out and with an AbortError when the task is cancelled; it throws GS-API-008 for a condition that is not a function, GS-API-011 for options that are not an object, GS-API-003 for a timeoutMs out of range and GS-API-017 for a retry out of range.

label: Binding
documentation: A binding made with bind(); dispose() stops it and puts the property back to its value from before the binding. Bindings made inside a task stop when that task ends, those made at module top level last as long as the script.

label: ControlEvent
documentation: What a control listener receives: the cancel signal and the id of the control.

label: DirectionEvent
documentation: What onDirectionChange receives: the new direction in degrees.

label: CellEvent
documentation: What a direction wheel's onChoose receives: the cell picked, counted from 0 at the first cell going clockwise.

label: WheelChoice
documentation: What an action wheel's onChoose receives: the cell run, counted from 0 at the top going clockwise, and its name.

label: VarChange
documentation: What a variable listener receives: the cancel signal, the variable id and its new value.

label: KeyEvent
documentation: What a key listener receives: the key's name, and on release how long it was held.

label: Keys
documentation: Keys by name, as in profiles ("KeyF", "Space", "Mouse.Left") or short (F, Esc, MouseLeft, WheelUp, GamepadA).

label: GlobalChange
documentation: What a global listener receives: the name and the new value.

label: ForegroundApp
documentation: The app in front on the phone: its package and whether Android calls it a game.

label: InputBox
documentation: An input box on the phone: whether it is open, its kind as Android's InputType number (1 text, 2 number, 3 phone, 4 date and time, with the variation and flag bits added), what its Enter key does and whether it takes several lines. When it closes the other fields are 0, "unspecified" and false.

label: LaunchOptions
documentation: Whether to stop the app before starting it.

label: ProfileInfo
documentation: A profile's id and name.

label: Work
documentation: Something to run: a Promise, or a function to start.

label: ConfirmOptions
documentation: The words on the two buttons of a yes or no question (up to 60 characters each).

label: AskOptions
documentation: The text already in the box when the question opens.

label: PicturePoint
documentation: A position on the phone picture as ratios: (0, 0) top left, (1, 1) bottom right.

label: InputName
documentation: A key or mouse button, written as in profiles, such as "KeyW", "ShiftLeft" or "Mouse.Right".

label: DrawColor
documentation: The colors a drawing can use; they follow the program's theme.

label: BoxOptions
documentation: A box's color (accent by default), a label of up to 60 characters and how long it stays, in milliseconds.

label: TextOptions
documentation: The text's color (accent by default) and how long it stays, in milliseconds.

label: MarkOptions
documentation: A mark's color (accent by default), a label of up to 60 characters shown to the right of the ring and how long it stays, in milliseconds.

label: Drawing
documentation: Something drawn on the picture; dispose() removes it. At most 64 are shown at a time.

label: Region
documentation: Part of the picture, as ratios: left, top, width and height.

label: FindOptions
documentation: Where to look (a region or a region name; the whole picture by default), how alike it must be from 0 to 1 (0.8 by default), how to compare (grey by default), how many to return for findAll (16 by default, at most 64) and how long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000). A template name brings its own threshold, match mode and region; options given here win.

label: Found
documentation: Where a picture was found: x and y are its center and width and height its size, as ratios of the picture; score is how alike it is, from 0 to 1.

label: WaitOptions
documentation: Where to look and how alike it must be, as for find(); timeoutMs is how long to keep looking in all (10000 ms by default, at most 600000) and intervalMs how long to wait between looks (250 ms by default, from 50 to 60000).

label: WatchOptions
documentation: Where to look and how alike it must be, as for find(); intervalMs is how long to wait between looks (500 ms by default, from 50 to 60000), and again what happens when the picture comes or goes again while the last task it started is still running.

label: MatchMode
documentation: How a template is compared. "grey" compares brightness only (zero-mean normalized cross-correlation). "color" also compares colors: the score is multiplied by 1 - d / 128 (at least 0), where d is the mean absolute difference of red, green and blue (0 to 255) over the template's opaque pixels, so the same shape in another color scores low.

label: ColorOptions
documentation: Where to look (the whole picture by default), how far each of red, green and blue may be from the color as a ratio of 255 (0.1 by default) and how long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000). A color name brings its own tolerance and region; options given here win.

label: PixelOptions
documentation: How long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000).

label: ChangeOptions
documentation: How much must change to count, as the share of the region from 0 to 1 (0.05 by default; a spot counts when its brightness moves by about a tenth or more), and how long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000).

label: OnChangeOptions
documentation: How much must change, as for changed(); intervalMs is how long to wait between looks (500 ms by default, from 50 to 60000), and again what happens when it changes again while the last task it started is still running.

label: ReadTextOptions
documentation: Where to read (a region or a region name; the whole picture by default), the language as a tag such as "zh-Hans" or "en" (by default the first Windows display language that has text recognition, otherwise the first one this computer has; findText looks for text of English letters, digits and signs with English recognition when the computer has it) and how long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000).

label: TextResult
documentation: Text read from the picture: text is every line joined with line breaks, lines each line with its place from top to bottom, and language the tag of the language it was read in, such as "zh-Hans-CN".

label: TextLine
documentation: One line of text: x and y are its center and width and height its size, as ratios of the picture.

label: PixelMatchOptions
documentation: How far each of red, green and blue may be from the color as a ratio of 255 (0.1 by default; a color name brings its own) and how long to wait while there is no picture yet (2000 ms by default, at most 10000).

label: PicturePath
documentation: A path on the picture: its points as ratios and how long a swipe along it takes, in milliseconds.

label: ImagePath
documentation: A picture in the profile folder, written as a relative path such as "res/chest.png".

label: HexColor
documentation: A color written "#RRGGBB", such as "#F5C542".

label: TemplateName
documentation: The name of a template in res/resources.json.

label: RegionName
documentation: The name of a region in res/resources.json.

label: PointName
documentation: The name of a point in res/resources.json.

label: PathName
documentation: The name of a path in res/resources.json.

label: ColorName
documentation: The name of a color in res/resources.json.

label: UiEventType
documentation: What the user does in a panel.

label: UiEvent
documentation: What a panel or menu listener receives: the id of the node or item, and its new value or null.

label: UiTone
documentation: The colors of text and icons in a panel; they follow the program's theme.

label: UiColor
documentation: A color in a chart or canvas: "#RRGGBB", or the name of a theme color such as "accent", "textPrimary" or "success".

label: UiNode
documentation: A node of a panel tree. A tree is at most 256 KiB as JSON, 2000 nodes and 16 levels deep.

label: UiColumn
documentation: Nodes one under another.

label: UiRow
documentation: Nodes side by side, going on in the next line when the panel is too narrow.

label: UiGroup
documentation: Nodes in a card with a title.

label: UiText
documentation: Text of up to 4000 characters. With markdown it shows **bold**, *italic*, `code` and lines that start with - or 1.; it never opens links or shows pictures.

label: UiButton
documentation: A button; a click sends click. icon is the name of a GameScrcpy icon.

label: UiField
documentation: A text box; leaving it sends change with the text, and Enter sends submit as well. The phone's keys pause while it has the keyboard.

label: UiNumber
documentation: A number box; a new number sends change.

label: UiToggle
documentation: A switch; flipping it sends change with true or false.

label: UiChoice
documentation: Up to 64 options to pick one from; picking sends change with the option's id.

label: UiOption
documentation: An option of a choice: text that is both its id and its title, or an id and a title.

label: UiSlider
documentation: A slider from min (0 if left out) to max (1 if left out); letting it go sends change with the value.

label: UiList
documentation: A list of up to 500 items; clicking one sends select with its id, unless selectable is false.

label: UiListItem
documentation: An item of a list.

label: UiTable
documentation: A table of up to 16 columns and 200 rows.

label: UiTableRow
documentation: A row of a table, one cell for each column.

label: UiCell
documentation: A cell of a table.

label: UiChart
documentation: A line or bar chart of up to 4 series; height is from 60 to 480, and min and max fix the scale.

label: UiSeries
documentation: A series of a chart: up to 500 values from left to right.

label: UiCanvas
documentation: A drawing of up to 500 shapes. width and height, from 1 to 2000, are in the panel's units; a wider drawing is made smaller to fit.

label: UiShape
documentation: A shape of a canvas: rect (x, y, width, height, radius), circle (x, y, radius), line (x1, y1, x2, y2), polyline (points as x, y, x, y… and closed) or text (x, y, text, size, color); fill, stroke and strokeWidth paint it.

label: UiImage
documentation: A PNG or SVG picture of up to 2 MiB in the extension's folder, written as a relative path; nothing outside the folder is shown.

label: UiProgress
documentation: A progress bar from 0 to 1; while value is null or left out it moves on its own.

label: UiSeparator
documentation: A thin line between nodes.

label: UiStatusNode
documentation: A status widget: a row or a single part, at most 64 nodes.

label: UiStatusRow
documentation: Parts of a status widget side by side.

label: UiStatusPart
documentation: A part of a status widget; its text is at most 100 characters.

label: UiStatusIcon
documentation: A GameScrcpy icon by its name.

label: UiMenuItem
documentation: An item of the right-click menu; with checked it shows a check mark, and picking it sends the opposite.

label: UiDeviceItem
documentation: A device in a list: its icon, name and a line under it, with a pill for its state; stateText words the pill. icon is the name of a GameScrcpy icon or "svg:" and the path of an SVG in the extension's folder. With an id, clicking it sends click.

label: UiSteps
documentation: The steps of something done in turn, 2 to 8 titles of up to 40 characters: those before current are done, current is going on (or went wrong with failed), and current equal to the number of steps means all are done.

label: UiQr
documentation: A QR code of up to 1000 bytes of text for a phone to scan.

label: UiKeyValue
documentation: Up to 100 rows of a name and its value.

label: UiKeyValueRow
documentation: A row of a keyValue: a name of up to 60 characters and its value.

label: UiToolbarState
documentation: What a toolbar button shows in place of what the manifest declares: its tooltip, its icon (a GameScrcpy icon or "svg:" and a path), whether it shows as on, and whether it can be clicked.

label: UiTarget
documentation: The card a menu was opened on: a device by its serial or a profile by its id, with its name.

label: UiChooseEvent
documentation: What a card menu listener receives: the item's id, its new checked state or null, and the card.

label: HardwareKind
documentation: The kinds of device logic can use: serial ports, USB HID devices and Bluetooth LE devices.

label: HardwareFilter
documentation: What a listed device must have: USB vendor and product ids and HID usage page and usage (0 to 65535), one of the Bluetooth service UUIDs, and how its name starts (up to 64 characters). A device is listed when it matches any one filter.

label: HardwareRequest
documentation: Which devices hardware.request() lists: one kind and up to 16 filters.

label: HardwareInfo
documentation: An allowed device: the id to open it with, its kind and name and, in hardware.list(), whether it is connected now.

label: HardwareClaimOptions
documentation: wait asks whoever holds the hardware to let it go and waits up to 3 seconds for it. onWanted is called with the name of whoever wants the hardware this logic holds; return true to let it go, and it is released for them.

label: NetListenOptions
documentation: Up to 16 sites, such as "https://example.com", whose pages may call the server from a browser; pages from the server itself and local files always may.

label: NetRequest
documentation: A request to a server of net.listen(): the path without the query, the query and headers (names in lowercase), and the body as text, bytes or parsed JSON. Bodies are up to 1 MiB.

label: NetAnswer
documentation: The answer to a request: a status (200 by default), headers, and text, JSON or bytes as the body; a text alone answers 200 with it, and nothing answers 204. The answer must come within 10 seconds.

label: SpeechSayOptions
documentation: engine is the id of an engine from speech.engines(); voice is the id or name of one of its voices; rate goes from 0.5 to 2, 1 being the voice's usual pace, and volume from 0 to 1. interrupt cuts off what the engine is reading and drops what waits, so that this text comes at once.

label: SpeechVoicesOptions
documentation: The id of an engine from speech.engines().

label: SpeechListenOptions
documentation: engine is the id of an engine from speech.engines() that listens; language is one of its languages, such as "zh-CN" or "en-US"; confidence, from 0 to 1, is how sure the engine must be before the handler runs.

label: SpeechHeard
documentation: A command that was heard: the phrase of the list it matched (null when the engine took any words), the words as the engine wrote them, and how sure it is, from 0 to 1.

label: SpeechVoice
documentation: A voice: the id or the name to pass as voice, and its language, such as "zh-CN".

label: SpeechEngineInfo
documentation: A speech engine: "system" is Windows, the others are "extension id/name". say and listen tell what it can do, dictation whether it takes any words rather than only a list of commands, and languages the languages it listens in.

label: HardwareBytes
documentation: Bytes to send: a Uint8Array, another typed array or a list of numbers from 0 to 255.

label: SerialOptions
documentation: How a serial port talks: 115200 baud (50 to 4000000), 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit and no flow control unless given, with the DTR and RTS lines on.

label: SerialSignals
documentation: The DTR and RTS lines of a serial port to turn on or off; the lines left out stay as they are.

label: BleService
documentation: A service of a Bluetooth LE device and its characteristics.

label: BleCharacteristic
documentation: A characteristic and what it allows: read, write, writeWithoutResponse, notify and indicate.

label: BleWriteOptions
documentation: Whether a write waits for the device to confirm it (true unless given).

label: DeviceDataEvent
documentation: What onData receives: the bytes that came in.

label: DeviceReportEvent
documentation: What onReport receives: the report id and the bytes after it.

label: DeviceNotifyEvent
documentation: What a subscription receives: the service and characteristic UUIDs, written in full, and the new value.

label: DeviceCloseEvent
documentation: Why a device closed by itself: it went away, Windows reported an error, or the permission to use it was taken back.

label: AiAskOptions
documentation: What ai.ask() sends along and how long it waits: picture true for the whole phone picture, a region or the name of one for that part of it, false or nothing for no picture; timeoutMs from 1000 to 120000 milliseconds, 60000 by default.

label: MediaFrameOptions
documentation: How media.frames() takes frames: at most fps a second, from 0.1 to 10 (2 by default); the long side at most size pixels, a whole number from 64 to 1920 (640 by default); only region, a part of the picture in ratios, when it is given.

label: ConvertInput
documentation: What a converter of an extension receives: the name of the file, the formats it converts from and to, and the contents as bytes, as text read as UTF-8, or parsed by json(). A converter is the export named convert, or the default export, of the script that contributes.converters names; it runs in the logic sandbox without a phone and returns a ConvertOutput. A profile comes as its JSON file, a task as its task.ts and a recording as its session.json. At most 32 MiB go in and at most 32 MiB come out, and a conversion may take 30 seconds; the message of what it throws is what the user sees. The conversion fails with GS-API-165 when the script exports no such function, GS-API-166 when the result is not something GameScrcpy can write, and GS-API-167 when the result is larger than 32 MiB.

label: ConvertOutput
documentation: What a converter returns: the new file as bytes, as a text written as UTF-8 or as a JSON value written as JSON text, and for an import the name of the file, which names the new profile. A converter may also return the text, the bytes or the JSON value itself, such as the object of a profile; an object counts as a ConvertOutput when it has bytes, text or json. GameScrcpy checks what it imports as it checks any file it imports.

label: VisionKind
documentation: What a recognition engine recognizes: text, things, or what the picture shows.

label: VisionParams
documentation: What a recognition engine takes besides the picture. "system" takes language, a tag such as "en" or "zh-Hans" (the languages of the user's profile by default), and words, true for each word instead of each line.

label: VisionEngineInfo
documentation: A recognition engine: "system" is Windows, the others are "extension id/name". kinds tells what it recognizes and languages the languages it reads, when it says.

label: VisionText
documentation: Text an engine read: x and y are its middle and width and height its size, as ratios of the picture; confidence goes from 0 to 1.

label: VisionObject
documentation: A thing an engine found: what it is, where it is as for VisionText, and how sure the engine is, from 0 to 1.

label: VisionClass
documentation: What an engine says the picture shows, and how sure it is, from 0 to 1.

label: VisionResult
documentation: One thing recognize() found: a VisionText for "ocr", a VisionObject for "detect" and a VisionClass for "classify".
